summary.headline: Deccan Gold turned debt-free after Rs.315 Cr rights issue; Jonnagiri gold sales and Geomysore profit flowed in, but Kyrgyz project needs Rs.60-100 Cr more.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a defining quarter: Rs.315 Cr rights issue used to repay about Rs.219 Cr of debt, leaving the company debt-free by end-March. The associate Geomysore (26% stake, Jonnagiri gold project) began selling refined gold and reported profit, which management said flowed into Deccan's books. Kyrgyzstan (60%) gravity circuit is commissioned, with Merrill-Crowe/leach circuit targeted for June-July and full-scale commercial production in August 2026. Management disclosed a funding gap after Rs.55 Cr was diverted to Geomysore's rights issue, and said it is talking to promoter-linked investors for Rs.60-100 Cr; an EGM on related-party transactions is scheduled. Bhalukona nickel-copper-PGE drilling is showing wide mineralised intersections, with mining lease application targeted by April 2027.

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, 26%)
segments.commentary: Open pit operating at 1,000 tpd licence capacity (about 300,000 tpa), recovery above 90%; FY27 production guided at about 600 kg, FY28 about 800 kg-1 t; FY27 revenue about Rs.900 Cr, EBITDA about Rs.630 Cr, PAT about Rs.470 Cr, with Deccan's 26% share about Rs.120 Cr, though management expects no dividend in FY27.

segments.name: Altyn Tor, Kyrgyzstan (60%, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Gravity concentrate production started; Merrill-Crowe and leach circuit to produce doré from June, full commercial production by August 2026. FY27 production guided at about 160 kg and FY28 at 300-350 kg; FY27 revenue about Rs.300 Cr, PAT about Rs.100 Cr (Deccan share about Rs.60 Cr). Processes about 1.6 Mt tailings and low-grade stockpiles (about 1-1.1 g/t) for about four years; 17% revenue share with Kyrgyzaltyn and 5% royalty to government.

segments.name: Bhalukona, Chhattisgarh (100%, nickel-copper-PGE)
segments.commentary: Seven diamond holes, 1,200 m drilled; first hole intersected about 30 m of sulphide mineralisation (about 0.4% Ni), including 2.6 m at 1.01% Ni, 0.29% Cu and 0.2 g/t Pd. Management's indicative resource is 75,000-80,000 t nickel-equivalent and about 7-8 t gold-equivalent, unverified.

segments.name: Ganajur (Karnataka)
segments.commentary: Gold deposit under litigation (High Court and Supreme Court, Indocil case); no ruling in the quarter. Management said timeline to production is about 2.5-3 years if the case is won.

segments.name: Gold-tungsten-tin, Spain (Logrosan)
segments.commentary: MoU to acquire 51% for EUR1.76 million with rights to go to 95%; 4 holes and about 1,500 m drilled, assays pending about 1-2 weeks. Earlier historic hole: 1 m at 96.2 g/t Au.

segments.name: Kalevala Gold, Finland
segments.commentary: Three projects (Syrjala about 2 Mt resource targeted to 4 t, Pahkalampi about 2 t at 3.5 g/t, 4P undrilled); company can go to 51%. Little work done this year due to funding constraints.

segments.name: Mozambique and Tanzania
segments.commentary: Mozambique lithium-tantalum surface targets identified, drilling deferred for lack of funds. Tanzania: three of five tenements relinquished, exploration focus reduced.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated targets (at current prices): Jonnagiri about 600 kg, Kyrgyzstan about 160 kg; FY28 Jonnagiri about 800 kg-1 t, Kyrgyzstan 300-350 kg.
Kyrgyzstan full-scale commercial production by August 2026; plant inauguration pencilled for 15 or 31 August.
Management funding need: at least Rs.60 Cr (outer limit Rs.100 Cr) for Kyrgyzstan; Rs.400-500 Cr for Bhalukona processing plant; Rs.800-1,000 Cr aggregate across projects in the next year or so.
Bhalukona mining lease application due by about April 2027; Spain mining lease application by October-November 2026.
2030 vision: Jonnagiri 1 tpa, Altyn Tor 700-800 kg, first Indian nickel-copper-PGE mine, and two to three gold mines plus critical minerals in production.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri 1,000 tpd plant capex about Rs.350-400 Cr; Bhalukona processing plant about Rs.400 Cr; Spain about Rs.500 Cr (Finland underground would need more).
Kyrgyzstan underground development (decline) estimated at Rs.50-100 Cr, starting after three to four years, to be funded from internal accruals per management.
Jonnagiri expansion beyond 2,000 tpd needs public hearing and permits; clarity expected in 6-8 months, reflected in FY28 numbers.
Kyrgyzstan revised resource estimate to state reserve company by end-June; revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by August 2026.
Bhalukona: 2,000-3,000 tpd plant potentially, 15-year life, if resource is proven to 200 m depth.
demand_pricing: Model assumptions: gold about Rs.15,000/g for Jonnagiri and about $4,000/oz for Kyrgyzstan, a discount to spot. Management said there is no hedging policy.
Royalties: Jonnagiri pays 4% to Andhra Pradesh plus 1.28% (DMF and NMET), about 5.28% of top line; Kyrgyzstan 5% royalty plus 17% revenue share to Kyrgyzaltyn.
Jonnagiri refined 999 gold sold to bullion refiners and jewellers at IBJA price; Kyrgyz doré must be sold to National Bank (right of first refusal) at LBMA price less refining charges.
Bhalukona concentrate expected to be sold to smelters (Adani or Vedanta named); management said crude-price impact on Kyrgyz costs is under 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income so high and what is its breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs.18.3 Cr is interest income on the Kyrgyz loan at 15% and the balance is currency exchange gain, totalling about Rs.31 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the Rs.100 Cr needed in the next three months, and can it come from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.100 Cr is an outer limit; actual need is about Rs.60 Cr over two to three years. Geomysore dividends may not come in FY27, so the company is talking to promoter-linked investors for debt or equity.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the promoters providing funds, and is any promoter selling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funding is from key promoter-group investors and an Australian promoter; Yandal Investments (about 10%) and Halcyon (about 5%) are not selling, with sales coming from retail promoter-group holders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Bhalukona mining lease and what could be the next production asset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mining lease application is due by about April 2027, with plant design then and production possibly around 2029; Bhalukona is the next candidate, with Spain also filing by Oct-Nov 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is an FPO or preferential issue planned and is the team ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has been in touch with merchant bankers and FPO planning would follow the present projects; it committed to nothing specific on timing.

risks_watch: Kyrgyz funding gap of Rs.60-100 Cr must close before winter construction; a bank transfer delay of a month would push completion months later.
Ganajur litigation outcome is unresolved; management is pursuing government policy routes.
Geomysore dividends not expected in FY27, so Deccan's Rs.120 Cr PAT share may not translate into cash; Kyrgyz loan repayments with 15% interest depend on production starting.
Bhalukona and Spain drill assays are pending and the Bhalukona resource figures are management's own geological estimates, not a JORC resource.
Gold price assumptions are below spot, but there is no hedging policy; a sharp fall in gold prices would hit revenue projections directly.
Management confirmed that Jonnagiri's FY27 revenue and profit forecasts assume about 600 kg; delays have occurred in past timelines.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on project potential (Bhalukona described as a personal favourite, Jonnagiri as transformational), but cautious on funding and timelines, repeatedly saying figures are indicative and not committing to dates. Evasive on several questions: no concrete answer on Geomysore IPO or reverse merger, and deferred the FPO question to after project milestones.
key_quotes: One of our associate companies that is Geomysore has recorded a profit and we could show some profit as a 26% shareholder of that Company.
We repaid all the debt that is about Rs.219 crores.
So we require up to Rs.100 Crores at least minimum Rs.60 Crores we require to complete that Kyrgyz project.
So by next April, we have to submit the mining lease application.
Rs.100 Crores is the completely outer limit that we are taking in case of any emergencies, but the actual requirement is around Rs.60 Crores.

Jonnagiri 1,000 tpd open pit operating at licence capacity (~300,000 tpa); FY27 target ~600 kg
Bhalukona processing plant (~2,000-3,000 tpd potential, not yet approved)

growth.why: FY27 gold output guided at ~600 kg Jonnagiri (via Geomysore, 26%) and ~160 kg Kyrgyzstan (60%), with Kyrgyz full-scale production by August 2026, but the Rs.60-100 Cr Kyrgyz funding gap is not yet closed and no revenue growth percentage was stated.
